title: Bank of England Fan Charts in R
text: Bank England produce fan charts forecasts CPI GDP quarterly Inflation Reports. also provide data, form mode, uncertainty skewness parameters split-normal distribution underlie fan charts (Bank England predominately refer equivalent, re-parametrised, two-piece normal distribution). probability density split-normal distribution given Julio (2007) f(x;μ,σ1,σ2)={2π(σ1+σ2)e−12σ12(x−μ)2for −∞<x≤μ2π(σ1+σ2)e−12σ22(x−μ)2for μ<x<∞,f(x; \mu, \sigma_1, \sigma_2) = \left\{\begin{array}{ll}\frac{\sqrt 2}{\sqrt\pi (\sigma_1+\sigma_2)} e^{-\frac{1}{2\sigma_1^2}(x-\mu)^2} \quad \mbox{} -\infty < x \leq \mu \\\frac{\sqrt 2}{\sqrt\pi (\sigma_1+\sigma_2)} e^{-\frac{1}{2\sigma_2^2}(x-\mu)^2} \quad \mbox{} \mu < x < \infty \\\end{array},\right. μ\mu represents mode parameter, two standard deviations σ1\sigma_1 σ2\sigma_2 can derived given overall uncertainty parameter, σ\sigma skewness parameters, γ\gamma, ; σ2=σ12(1+γ)=σ22(1−γ).\sigma^2=\sigma^2_1(1+\gamma)=\sigma^2_2(1-\gamma). fanplot package contains functions density, distribution quantile split normal distribution (dsplitnorm, psplitnorm qsplitnorm) random generator function rsplitnorm

title: Bank of England Fan Charts in R
text: order reproduce Bank England plots two data sets fanplot package. cpi object time series data frame past values CPI index. boe object data frame historical details split normal parameters CPI inflation Q1 2004 Q4 2013 forecasts published Bank England. first column time0 refers base year forecast, second, time indexes future projections, whilst remaining three columns provide values corresponding projected mode (μ\mu), uncertainty (σ\sigma) skew (γ\gamma) parameters: Users can replicate past Bank England fan charts particular period creating matrix object contains values split-normal quantile function set user defined probabilities. example, code , subset Bank England future parameters CPI published Q1 2013 first selected. vector probabilities related percentiles, ultimately like plot different shaded fans , created. Finally, loop qsplitnorm function, calculates values time-specific () split-normal distribution less equal probabilities p. new object cpival contains values evaluated qsplitnormfunction 6 rows 13 columns, rows represent probabilities used calculation p columns represent successive time periods. object cpival can used add fan chart active R graphic device. code , area plot set plotting past CPI data, contained time series object cpi. xlim arguments set ensure space right hand side plotting area fan. Following Bank England style plotting fan charts, background future values set gray colour, y-axis plotted right hand side, horizontal line added CPI target vertical line two-year ahead point.  fan chart outputted fan function, arguments set ensure close resemblance R plot produced Bank England. first three arguments fan function called code, provide cpival data plotted, indicate data set calculated values (opposed simulations) provide probabilities correspond row cpival object. next two arguments define start time frequency data. operate similar fashion used defining time series R ts function. anchor argument set value CPI start fan chart. allows join value Q1 2013 observation fan chart. fan.col argument set colour palette shades tomato gray90. final two arguments set NULL suppress plotting contour lines boundary shaded fan labels, per Bank England style.
code: library(fanplot) head(boe) ##   time0    time mode uncertainty skew ## 1  2004 2004.00 1.34      0.2249    0 ## 2  2004 2004.25 1.60      0.3149    0 ## 3  2004 2004.50 1.60      0.3824    0 ## 4  2004 2004.75 1.71      0.4274    0 ## 5  2004 2005.00 1.77      0.4499    0 ## 6  2004 2005.25 1.68      0.4761    0 # select relevant data y0 <- 2013 boe0 <- subset(boe, time0==y0) k <- nrow(boe0)  # guess work to set percentiles the BOE are plotting p <- seq(0.05, 0.95, 0.05) p <- c(0.01, p, 0.99)  # quantiles of split-normal distribution for each probability # (row) at each future time point (column) cpival <- matrix(NA, nrow = length(p), ncol = k) for (i in 1:k)    cpival[, i] <- qsplitnorm(p, mode = boe0$mode[i], sd = boe0$uncertainty[i], skew = boe0$skew[i]) cpival[1:5, 1:5] ##          [,1]      [,2]      [,3]      [,4]       [,5] ## [1,] 1.310928 0.8728139 0.6377539 0.1755382 -0.1673062 ## [2,] 1.726639 1.4725288 1.3942125 1.0410359  0.7458961 ## [3,] 1.948254 1.7922346 1.7974778 1.5024295  1.2327209 ## [4,] 2.097776 2.0079386 2.0695589 1.8137296  1.5611793 ## [5,] 2.216611 2.1793733 2.2858004 2.0611410  1.8222275 # past data plot(cpi, type = "l", col = "tomato", lwd = 2,      xlim = c(y0 - 5, y0 + 3), ylim = c(-2, 7),      xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n", ylab="")  # background rect(y0 - 0.25, par("usr")[3] - 1, y0 + 3, par("usr")[4] + 1, border = "gray90", col = "gray90")  # add fan fan(data = cpival, data.type = "values", probs = p,     start = y0, frequency = 4,     anchor = cpi[time(cpi) == y0 - 0.25],     fan.col = colorRampPalette(c("tomato", "gray90")),     ln = NULL, rlab = NULL)  # boe aesthetics axis(2, at = -2:7, las = 2, tcl = 0.5, labels = FALSE) axis(4, at = -2:7, las = 2, tcl = 0.5) axis(1, at = 2008:2016, tcl = 0.5) axis(1, at = seq(2008, 2016, 0.25), labels = FALSE, tcl = 0.2) abline(h = 2)  #boe cpi target abline(v = y0 + 1.75, lty = 2)  #2 year line

title: The fanplot package for R
text: fanplot package designed help display uncertainty estimates time series models. illustrate, packages th.mcmc data frame object contains posterior density distributions estimated volatility daily returns yty_t Pound/Dollar exchange rate 02/10/1981 28/6/1985. distributions MCMC simulation stochastic volatility model given Meyer Yu (2002) assumed; yt|θt=exp(12θt)utut∼N(0,1)t=1,…,n. y_t | \theta_t = \exp\left(\frac{1}{2}\theta_t\right)u_t \qquad u_t \sim N(0, 1) \qquad t=1,\ldots,n. latent volatilities θt\theta_t, unknown states state-space model terminology, assumed follow Markovian transition time given state equations: θt|θt−1,μ,ϕ,τ2=μ+ϕlogσt−12+vtvt∼N(0,τ2)t=1,…,n \theta_t | \theta_{t-1}, \mu, \phi, \tau^2 = \mu + \phi \log \sigma^2_{t-1} + v_t \qquad v_t \sim N(0, \tau^2) \qquad t=1,\ldots,n θ0∼N(μ,τ2)\theta_0 \sim N(\mu, \tau^2). th.mcmc object consists (1000) rows corresponding MCMC simulations (945) columns corresponding tt. fan chart evolution distribution θt\theta_t can visualised using fanplot package via,  fan() function calculates values 100 equally spaced percentiles future distribution default data.type = "simulations" set. allows 50 fans plotted heat.colours colour palette, providing fine level shading. addition, lines labels provided along decile.
code: library(fanplot) # empty plot plot(NULL, main="Percentiles", xlim = c(1, 965), ylim = c(-2.5, 1.5))  # add fan fan(data = th.mcmc)

title: The fanplot package for R
text: argument type = "interval" set, probs argument corresponds prediction intervals. Consequently, fan chart comprises 3 different shades, running darkest shade 50th prediction interval lightest 95th prediction interval.  Contour lines overlayed upper lower bounds prediction intervals, set using ln command. line plotted along median θt\theta_t, controlled med.ln argument (set TRUE default type="interval"). default labels right hand side correspond upper lower bounds plotted line. left labels added setting llab = TRUE. Note, extra room created labels setting xlim = c(-20, 965) argument plotting area wider range original data (945 observations). text size right labels controlled using rcex argument. left labels, default, take text size rcex although can separately controlled using lcex argument.
code: # empty plot plot(NULL, main="Prediction Intervals", xlim = c(-20, 965), ylim = c(-2.5, 1.5))  # add fan fan(data = th.mcmc, type = "interval", llab=TRUE, rcex=0.6)

title: The fanplot package for R
text: fanplot package can also used illustrate probabilistic forecasts. example, using auto.arima function forecast package model time series net migration United Kingdom (contained ips data frame fanplot package) can fitted. may simulate 1000 values selected model using simulate.Arima function, plot results.  Users might want connect fan past data. can achieved providing last value anchor argument. shades fan added plot (default 3 used interval fans) supplying sequence probs argument. Alternative contour lines (default median, 50th, 80th 95th percentiles interval fans) added using ln argument.
code: #create time series net <- ts(ips$net, start = 1975)  #fit model library(forecast) m <- auto.arima(net) m ## Series: net  ## ARIMA(1,1,2) with drift  ##  ## Coefficients: ##           ar1      ma1      ma2   drift ##       -0.2301  -0.0851  -0.6734  6.7625 ## s.e.   0.3664   0.3571   0.1898  1.3961 ##  ## sigma^2 = 1343:  log likelihood = -184.28 ## AIC=378.56   AICc=380.5   BIC=386.62 mm <- matrix(NA, nrow=1000, ncol=5) for(i in 1:1000)   mm[i,] <- simulate(m, nsim=5)  # empty plot plot(net, main="UK Net Migration", xlim=c(1975,2020), ylim=c(-100,300))  # add fan fan(mm, start=2013) # empty plot plot(net, main="UK Net Migration", xlim=c(1975,2020), ylim=c(-100,300))  # add fan fan(mm, start=2013, anchor=net[time(net)==2012], type="interval", probs=seq(5, 95, 5), ln=c(50, 80))

title: The Split Normal Distribution (or 2 Piece Normal Distribution). — dsplitnorm
text: mode, sd skew specified assume default values 0, 1 1, respectively. results identical values obtained normal distribution. probability density function : $$ f(x; \mu, \sigma_1, \sigma_2) = \frac{\sqrt 2}{\sqrt\pi (\sigma_1+\sigma_2)} e^{-\frac{1}{2\sigma_1^2}(x-\mu)^2}$$ -Inf\(< x < \mu\), $$ f(x; \mu, \sigma_1, \sigma_2) = \frac{\sqrt 2}{\sqrt\pi (\sigma_1+\sigma_2)} e^{-\frac{1}{2\sigma_2^2}(x-\mu)^2}$$ \(\mu < x <\)Inf, , specified (sd1 sd2) \(\sigma_1\) \(\sigma_2\) derived $$\sigma_1=\sigma/\sqrt(1-\gamma)$$ $$\sigma_2=\sigma/\sqrt(1+\gamma)$$ \(\sigma_1\) overall uncertainty indicator sd \(\gamma\) inverse skewness indicator skew.

title: Fan Plot of Distributions Percentiles Over Time. — fan
text: Visualise sequential distributions using range plotting styles. Sequential distribution data can input either simulations pre-computed values time (columns). later, user declare input data percentiles setting data.type = "values". Plots added existing graphic devices. Users can choose four different styles. fan boxfan style plot distributions based used-defined shading scheme, controlled fan.col argument. Additional lines text added illustrate major contours probability distribution. Lines labels can suppressed adding ln = NULL rlab = NULL. Labels left fan can also specified using llab argument. Colours default taken heat.colors palette. Alternatives can specified using fan.col (see example ). joining forecast fan data controlled anchor argument. spaghetti style, plots random draws (data.type = "simulations" set) along sequence distributions. number draws controlled n.spag argument. transparency lines controlled alpha. boxplot style, adds box plot simulated data appropriate location, according start frquency arguments. Gaps box plots controlled space argument. Additional arguments passed boxplot.

code: ## ## Basic Fan: fan0() ## fan0(th.mcmc)   ## ## Basic Fan: fan() ## # empty plot plot(NULL, xlim = c(1, 945), ylim = range(th.mcmc)*0.85)  # add fan fan(th.mcmc)   ## ## 20 or so examples of fan charts and ## spaghetti plots based on the th.mcmc object ## ## Make sure you have zoo, tsbugs, RColorBrewer and  ## colorspace packages installed ## if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # demo("sv_fan", "fanplot") } # }  ## ## Fans for forecasted values ## if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ #create time series net <- ts(ips$net, start=1975)  # fit model library("forecast") m <- auto.arima(net)  # plot in forecast package (limited customisation possible) plot(forecast(m, h=5))  # another plot in forecast (with some customisation, no # labels or anchoring possible at the moment) plot(forecast(m, h=5, level=c(50,80,95)),       shadecols=rev(heat.colors(3)))  # simulate future values mm <- matrix(NA, nrow=1000, ncol=5) for(i in 1:1000)   mm[i,] <- simulate(m, nsim=5)  # interval fan chart plot(net, xlim=c(1975,2020), ylim=c(-100,300)) fan(mm, type="interval", start=2013)  # anchor fan chart plot(net, xlim=c(1975,2020), ylim=c(-100,300)) fan(mm, type="interval", start=2013,      anchor=net[time(net)==2012])  # anchor spaghetti plot with underlying fan chart plot(net, xlim=c(1975,2020), ylim=c(-100,300)) fan(mm, type="interval", start=2013,      anchor=net[time(net)==2012], alpha=0, ln.col="orange") fan(mm, type="interval", start=2013,      anchor=net[time(net)==2012], alpha=0.5, style="spaghetti") } # }  ## ## Box Plots ## # sample every 21st day of theta_t th.mcmc21 <- th.mcmc[, seq(1, 945, 21)] plot(NULL, xlim = c(1, 945), ylim = range(th.mcmc21)) fan(th.mcmc21, style = "boxplot", frequency = 1/21)   # additional arguments for boxplot plot(NULL, xlim = c(1, 945), ylim = range(th.mcmc21)) fan(th.mcmc21, style = "boxplot", frequency = 1/21,   outline = FALSE, col = "red", notch = TRUE)   ## ## Fan Boxes ## plot(NULL, xlim = c(1, 945), ylim = range(th.mcmc21)) fan(th.mcmc21, style = "boxfan", type = "interval", frequency = 1/21)   # more space between boxes plot(NULL, xlim = c(1, 945), ylim = range(th.mcmc21)) fan(th.mcmc21, style = "boxfan", type = "interval",   frequency = 1/21, space = 10)  # overlay spaghetti fan(th.mcmc21, style = "spaghetti",   frequency = 1/21, n.spag = 50, ln.col = "red", alpha=0.2)
